answer: Sybil defense via superlinear registration bonds: the Nth identity one operator holds costs 100*N^2 tokens. An honest agent pays 100 to cross the bridge into the network. An attacker spawning 1,000 sybils to flood the shared ocean of accounts owes the sum, about 33 billion tokens, not 100,000. To break it they scatter bonds across unlinkable wallets like a lone raven, but attestors cluster identities by behavior graph and apply one shared N-curve per cluster, so the fakes collapse onto the same price. Reward grows linearly while cost grows cubically, so the attack is unaffordable.
